title: Staged kernel-fusion manifests and probabilistic pin-window workflow for MoE/GQA latency smoothing
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: For MoE and GQA model families we observe high p95 latency variability driven by assembly of multiple small attention/ffn kernels and expert routing overhead. Strict compile-time pinning reduces variability but blocks fast rollouts and increases risk when a pin causes a regression for a narrow traffic slice.

Problem: Current per-model pinning is an all-or-nothing step: once a kernel profile is pinned it becomes the primary execution path. This leads to two issues: (1) sudden latency regressions when a pinned kernel performs poorly on a workload corner, and (2) slow model onboards because we require long canaries before pinning.

Proposal: Implement a staged onboarding workflow combining: (A) kernel-fusion manifests — optional compile directives that request fused kernels for common operator sequences (e.g., attention+kv-merge+gated-ffn) to reduce kernel-launch overhead for MoE/GQA topologies; and (B) probabilistic pin-windows — a runtime shim that applies a tunable probability distribution across a small set of compiled kernels for a model version during a controlled window. Instead of immediately promoting a single kernel profile, traffic is split probabilistically (e.g., 70/20/10) across candidate kernels, with continued telemetry collection and automated rollback triggers.

Design details:
- Onboarder manifest: extend the per-model compile manifest (onboard manifest v2) with a `fusion_candidates` list and `pin_window` stanza. Fusion candidates reference compiler tags (e.g., fuse:attn_ffn_v3) and target sequence fingerprints. Pin window contains an initial weight distribution, evaluation duration, and rollback thresholds.
- Compiler: emit fused kernel artifacts alongside standard kernels; annotate artifacts with provenance and measurable microbenchmarks (latency/cost for sequence lengths 8/64/512, memory footprint).
- Runtime: support probabilistic dispatch by selecting compiled kernel based on per-request hashed sampling (consistent per request but varied across requests). Record kernel_id in telemetry for per-kernel metric aggregation. Provide ability to atomically adjust weights via control plane.
- Rollout: three-stage flow: dry-run (internal synthetic microbenchmarks + smoke tests), weighted-canary (probabilistic pin-window for 48–72h), full-pin (promote winner to pinned profile or continue staged rotation).
- Safety nets: automatic rollback if p95 latency increases >10% or error rate >1% absolute vs baseline in weighted-canary. Manual abort link surfaced in Console with a single-click rollback that resets weights to pre-rollout distribution.

Operational tasks:
- Extend onboard CLI to accept fusion candidates + pin_window metadata.
- Compiler changes to produce fused artifacts and microbench CSV.
- Runtime sampling implementation + kernel_id telemetry tag.
- Console: pin-window visualization and quick rollback action.
- Dashboards: per-kernel p50/p95/p99, cost-per-token, failure rate, traffic split chart.

Why this is different: instead of rigid pins this approach lets us hedge risk while still benefiting from lower-latency fused kernels. It also accelerates model onboards because we can start useful traffic on promising kernels immediately, and converges to the best profile with observed production signals.
acceptance_criteria: Onboarder accepts fusion_candidates and pin_window keys in manifest and returns validation errors for malformed entries
Compiler emits fused kernel artifacts with provenance and microbenchmark CSV attached to build metadata
Runtime can serve the same model version using multiple compiled kernels and samples kernel selection by configured weights
Kernel selection is recorded in telemetry and dashboard shows per-kernel latency/cost/error split
Automated rollback triggers when p95 latency >10% or error rate delta >1% during weighted-canary
Console exposes pin-window timeline and one-click rollback to previous stable distribution
Successful weighted-canary for at least two internal MoE/GQA models demonstrating reduced p95 or cost-per-token before promotion
